title: BNCI 2015-003 P300 dataset
description: EEG recordings from an online auditory P300 brain-computer interface speller based on the AMUSE (Auditory Multi-class Spatial ERP) paradigm. Healthy participants selected characters through a two-step hex-o-spell interface using spatial auditory cues from six speakers, with no visual stimulation. The dataset includes a fixed-iteration session and a session using dynamic stopping to speed up spelling.
methods_description: Participants sat surrounded by six speakers at ear height (60° spacing, 65 cm radius). Each direction had a unique tone and band-pass filtered noise combination. EEG was recorded from 8 Ag/AgCl channels with a BrainAmp amplifier at 256 Hz, referenced to the nose. Session 1 consisted of calibration (48 trials) followed by online spelling with 15 fixed iterations. Session 2 consisted of calibration followed by online spelling with dynamic stopping (4-15 iterations). Classification used spatio-temporal features with a shrinkage-regularized linear binary classifier.
